TASK 3: WORKSHOP SAFETY, TOOLS AND
SAFE VEHICLE SUPPORT
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 1 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 1-10
Your task
A mixed motor vehicle workshop practical is being prepared. You must inspect the work area, identify hazards, select
and check suitable tools and PPE, confirm the vehicle or training rig is safely supported, and record the controls
required before work begins.
What you must do
1
Confirm the practical activity, work area and limits of responsibility with the assessor.
2
Inspect the area, vehicle or rig and record hazards affecting people, equipment or the task.
3
Select and check the PPE, tools and equipment required for the planned activity.
4
Confirm vehicle support, battery, electrical and fire controls, stopping if any control is unsafe.
5
Explain the checks to the assessor, complete the record and leave the area safe and orderly.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Training vehicle, component, workshop rig or safe vehicle-support
demonstration area
PPE, hazard checklist and local workshop safety information
Hand tools, equipment and pre-use inspection checklist
Vehicle-support, battery, fire and technical information
Apprentice Assessment Record

60 minutes

Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 1-10
Your task
A vehicle component or workshop item requires inspection and accurate recording before specialist route training
begins. You must select suitable measuring equipment, interpret the relevant technical information, compare results
with the stated tolerance and complete a clear job-card handover.
What you must do
1
Confirm the item, required measurements and technical information with the assessor.
2
Inspect and select suitable measuring equipment, checking its condition and range.
3
Take and record the required measurements using the correct units and safe technique.
4
Compare the results with the specification or tolerance and identify any required action.
5
Complete the job card and give the assessor a clear handover of findings and recommendations.

Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.

A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.

precisely.

supported by evidence.

TASK 3: SUBSTRATE IDENTIFICATION AND
REPAIR METHOD SELECTION
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 2 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 11-28
Your task
A damaged vehicle has several panel areas made from different materials. You must identify the substrate, confirm
the suitable repair/refinish route and record the controls required before preparation continues.
What you must do
1
Confirm the panel area and inspect it without causing further damage.
2
Identify the substrate using safe visual and approved checking methods.
3
Consult product or OEM information to select the correct repair approach.
4
Record any restrictions such as aluminium control, plastic adhesion or composite referral.
5
Explain your chosen method and evidence to the assessor.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Vehicle panels or substrate sample set
OEM or product technical information
Identification charts, magnets, inspection lamp and PPE
Repair method selection worksheet
Apprentice Assessment Record
SOW ALIGNMENT

TASK 4: FEATHER EDGING, FILLER
PREPARATION AND PRIMER READINESS
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 2 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 11-28
Your task
A repaired area requires controlled feather edging and surface preparation ready for filler or primer surfacer. You
must prepare the surface, check contour and record readiness for the next refinish stage.
What you must do
1
Confirm the repair area, substrate and limits of the preparation task.
2
Clean the area and select suitable abrasive grades for feather edging.
3
Prepare the surface gradually, maintaining panel shape and body lines.
4
Check the repair area for pinholes, low spots, contamination or poor edges.
5

Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 3 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT

Your task
A minor damage repair requires filler finishing and primer application. You must shape the repair, prepare for primer,
apply or plan primer application under supervision and complete quality checks before handover.
What you must do
1
Check the panel, job card and product data before starting work.
2
Shape the filler/stopper and prepare the surface to the required standard.
3
Mask the area and confirm primer material, ratio, flash-off and safety controls.
4
Apply primer under instruction or complete a supervised set-up and method plan.
5
Inspect the result, identify defects and record rework or next-stage actions.

precisely.

supported by evidence.

Abrasives, guide coat, masking materials and inspection lamp
QA checklist and job card

TASK 4: COMPLEX MASKING, CORROSION
PROTECTION AND SEAM SEALER CONTROL
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 3 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 29-42
Your task
A repaired vehicle section requires complex masking and protection before refinish work continues. You must mask
vulnerable areas, identify corrosion protection requirements and document seam sealer or stone chip considerations.
What you must do
1
Confirm the repair area and identify surfaces needing protection or product reinstatement.
2
Mask shuts, trims, adjacent panels and apertures using suitable materials.
3
Review product data for seam sealer, stone chip or corrosion protection where required.
4
Check masking edges, overspray risk, access and contamination controls before handover.
5
Record the completed work, product references and any further action required.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Vehicle section, repaired panel or training shell
Masking paper, film, tape, foam and trim protection materials
Seam sealer, stone chip or corrosion protection data sheets
Inspection lamp, PPE and extraction/ventilation controls
Job card and evidence capture device
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 3 - Fillers, Primers, Masking and Corrosion Protection
Duties: D1-D6, D8, D9 KSB evidence focus: K1-K4, K6-K9, S1-S5, B1, B2, B6

TASK 3: COLOUR CODE, VARIANT SELECTION
AND SPRAY-OUT CARD
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 4 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 43-56
Your task
A vehicle requires colour confirmation before refinishing. You must locate the colour code, compare variants, produce
or prepare a spray-out card process and record colour evidence for the job.
What you must do
1
Locate the vehicle colour code and confirm job-card details.
2
Use the colour retrieval system or formula information to identify variants.
3
Prepare a spray-out card method, or complete it under controlled supervision.
4
Compare the result under suitable lighting and record colour observations.
5
Explain your colour choice, blend recommendation and evidence to the assessor.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Vehicle or panel with identifiable colour information
Paint mixing scheme, formula sheets or colour retrieval system
Spray-out cards, panels, gun set-up sheet and PPE
Colour lamp or daylight viewing area where available
Job card and evidence record
SOW ALIGNMENT

Duties: D4, D5, D7, D10 KSB evidence focus: K1, K3, K6, K8, S3-S5, B4, B7

TASK 4: MIXING RATIOS, VISCOSITY, VOC AND
MATERIAL PLANNING
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 4 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 43-56
Your task
A refinishing job requires materials to be planned and mixed accurately. You must calculate material needs, confirm
ratios, consider viscosity and waste, and record how the mix supports compliance and quality.
What you must do
1
Confirm the repair area, product system and stage of refinish work.
2
Use product data to identify ratio, hardener/thinner options and pot life.
3
Calculate the estimated quantity needed and record any waste-control decisions.
4
Prepare or simulate the mix using the correct measuring method and controls.
5
Record the mix data, equipment used and any issues found during planning.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Paint product data sheets and mixing scheme information
Mixing cups, scales, viscosity cup where available and stirrers
Sample formula or simulated mixing materials
VOC/waste control information and PPE
Material planning record
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 4 - Colour Theory, Paint Mixing and Technical Data
Duties: D4, D5, D7, D10 KSB evidence focus: K1, K3, K6, K8, S3-S5, B4, B7

AND BOOTH CONTROLS
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 5 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 57-71
Your task
Before applying refinish material, the spray equipment and booth or training bay must be prepared. You must
complete equipment checks, set up the spray gun and record booth or ventilation controls.
What you must do
1
Confirm the material type, task stage and equipment required.
2
Inspect the spray gun, nozzle, cap, pot, air supply and filtration condition.
3
Set or record air pressure, fan pattern, fluid control and test pattern outcome.
4
Check booth or spray area controls, extraction, cleanliness and safety boundaries.
5
Record all settings, faults, corrective actions and evidence references.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Spray gun, air-line gauge, airline and filtration equipment
Paint booth, spray bay or training spray area
Test paper/panel, cleaning materials and PPE/RPE
Product or equipment data sheet
Set-up and QA record

Your task
A panel or test piece requires controlled application of basecoat and/or clearcoat. You must follow the material
process, monitor flash-off and curing conditions, and inspect for common application defects.
What you must do

Confirm product data, panel preparation and safety controls before application.
2
Apply or simulate the coating process using correct distance, angle and overlap.
3
Record coat sequence, flash-off times, booth or curing settings and observations.
4
Inspect the panel for dry spray, runs, poor coverage, dirt nibs or edge issues.
5
Record corrective actions, evidence and any next-stage recommendations.

information.

precisely.

supported by evidence.

applicable

Application and curing record

AND QA GATES
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 6 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT

Your task
A vehicle requires a full paint repair workflow from initial preparation through handover. You must plan the process,
identify handover points with panel/MET colleagues and build quality gates into the job.
What you must do
1
Review the job card, damage information, repair area and expected outcome.
2
Plan the sequence of paint operations and identify any dependencies or constraints.
3
Add quality gates for preparation, substrate check, colour, application and final inspection.
4
Prepare a handover note for colleagues or the next stage of repair.
5
Record evidence requirements, risks, delays and customer/update points.

SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.

A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.

Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.

TASK 4: PAINT DEFECT DIAGNOSIS, REWORK
PLAN AND EVIDENCE REVIEW
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 6 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 72-85
Your task
A finished panel has one or more paint defects. You must inspect the finish, identify likely root causes, plan
rectification and record evidence for quality improvement and portfolio use.
What you must do
1
Confirm the panel area and inspect the finish under suitable lighting.
2
Identify and record each defect using accurate paint terminology.
3
Link the likely root cause to preparation, mixing, application, curing or environment.
4
Produce a rectification plan, identifying when further supervision is required.
5
Record evidence references, learning points and actions to prevent recurrence.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Finished panel, defect samples or photograph-based scenario
Inspection lamps, defect guides and QA checklist
Flatting/polishing awareness materials where appropriate
Product data sheets and repair records
Portfolio evidence review sheet
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 6 - Process Integration, Productivity and Quality Control
Duties: D1, D5, D8, D9, D10 KSB evidence focus: K5-K9, S1, S3-S5, B1-B7
Task reference: Block_6_Task_4_Paint_Defect_Diagnosis_Rework_Plan_and_Evidence_Review

TASK 3: PLASTIC BUMPER PREPARATION AND
ADHESION SYSTEM
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 7 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 86-100
Your task
A plastic bumper or trim section requires preparation for refinishing. You must identify the plastic, prepare the
surface safely, choose the adhesion system and record the controls needed for a durable repair.
What you must do
1
Confirm the plastic component, repair area and required finish.
2
Clean and prepare the surface using product and task guidance.
3
Identify adhesion promoter, primer or flexibility requirements from technical data.
4
Check for contamination, static risk, edge quality and readiness for coating.
5
Record product choices, preparation method, QA findings and evidence references.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Plastic bumper/trim section or training panel
Plastic identification information and product data sheets
Cleaning materials, abrasives, antistatic cloths and PPE
Adhesion promoter or primer system information
QA checklist and job card
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 7 - Advanced Blending, Plastics and Defect Rectification
Duties: D2-D8, D10 KSB evidence focus: K1-K4, K6, K8, K9, S2-S5, B1, B6, B7
Task reference: Block_7_Task_3_Plastic_Bumper_Preparation_and_Adhesion_System

TASK 4: ADVANCED BLENDING, THREE-STAGE
COLOUR AND DEFECT RECTIFICATION
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 7 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 86-100
Your task
A repair requires an advanced blend or complex colour approach. You must plan the blend area, consider metallic,
mica or three-stage colour behaviour and identify how finish defects would be rectified.
What you must do
1
Review the colour information, repair position and possible blend areas.
2
Prepare a blend plan showing panel layout, masking strategy and fade-out control.
3
Record how colour, metallic/mica orientation or pearl coat control will be managed.
4
Inspect sample evidence or a finished panel and identify any correction action needed.
5
Explain blend decisions, risks and evidence to the assessor.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Prepared panels, spray-out cards or advanced colour scenario
Colour formula, variant data and product technical information
Blend mapping sheet, masking materials and inspection lighting
Defect examples or QA guide
Application/evidence record
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 7 - Advanced Blending, Plastics and Defect Rectification
Duties: D2-D8, D10 KSB evidence focus: K1-K4, K6, K8, K9, S2-S5, B1, B6, B7

FUEL PAINT SAFETY REFERRAL
Vehicle Damage Paint Technician Level 3 | Block 8 | v1.1
TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 101-114
Your task
A modern vehicle is entering the paint process. You must recognise EV/hybrid, ADAS or alternative-fuel risks, identify
safe paint-shop boundaries and record what must be referred before work continues.
What you must do
1
Review the vehicle/scenario and identify EV, hybrid, ADAS or alternative-fuel indicators.
2
Check whether paint preparation, masking, booth bake or refinish work may affect systems.
3
Identify safe boundaries and any activity requiring qualified referral or calibration advice.
4
Record restrictions, heat controls, sensor protection and customer/workshop updates.
5
Explain the referral decision and evidence to the assessor.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.

Vehicle, training vehicle, photos or modern-vehicle scenario cards
OEM information, warning labels and ADAS sensor location
information
EV/hybrid awareness guidance and PPE where appropriate
Paint booth/cure temperature information
Safety referral and job-card update sheet

TIME
60 minutes
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge | Documentation

Weeks 129-139
Your task
You are completing a mock integrated paint task under assessment-style conditions. You must plan, prepare,
complete the required paint process, inspect the outcome and explain your decisions with supporting evidence.
What you must do
1
Read the mock task brief and confirm the required outcome with the assessor.
2
Plan the process, PPE, materials, equipment and quality checks before starting.
3
Complete the preparation/application/inspection stages within the agreed task scope.
4
Record technical data, settings, defects, corrective actions and evidence references.
5
Reflect on performance and agree any final development actions.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE SETUP
Suitable PPE, a prepared work area and controlled vehicle,
component or equipment.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using the relevant procedure and technical
information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual readings, findings and actions recorded clearly and
precisely.
SOUND DECISIONS
Appropriate recommendations, referral or authorisation
supported by evidence.
You will need
Mock EPA paint repair scenario and job card
Vehicle/panel, materials, spray equipment, booth or training bay
Technical data, product sheets and safety information
QA checklist and observation record
Portfolio/evidence upload checklist
